issues.legal_issue: The statutory bar on benami-based title claims against a certified purchaser extends to persons claiming through that purchaser, and the exception for third-party claims does not cover transferees of the real purchaser.
material_facts: The alleged real purchaser acquired property at a court sale in the name of another person, who was the certified purchaser.
The plaintiff claimed the property through the alleged real purchaser, while the defendant claimed through the certified purchaser.
The plaintiff argued that the statutory exception for third-party claims applied because the alleged real purchaser had transferred the property to the plaintiff.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff’s benami-based claim was barred. The statutory protection extends to persons claiming through the certified purchaser, and the exception for third-party claims concerns creditors, not transferees.
issues.legal_principle: Section 66 of the Code of Civil Procedure bars a suit against a person claiming title under a court-certified purchase when the suit alleges that the purchase was made on behalf of the plaintiff or someone through whom the plaintiff claims. The section protects not only the certified purchaser but also persons claiming through that purchaser. Its second subsection concerns claims by creditors against property to satisfy a debt of the real owner; it does not permit a transferee of the alleged real purchaser to bring a benami-based title claim.

predicates.benami_based_title_suit: The plaintiff brings a suit seeking title on the ground that a court-certified purchase was made for the plaintiff or someone through whom the plaintiff claims.
predicates.plaintiff_claims_through_alleged_real_pu: The plaintiff claims the property through the person alleged to have been the real purchaser.
predicates.defendant_claims_through_certified_purch: The defendant claims title through the person named as purchaser in the court certificate.

issues.definition: When a benami-based title suit is brought by someone claiming through the alleged real purchaser against someone claiming through the certified purchaser, the claim is barred.

issues.legal_issue: A person whose possession has matured into title by adverse possession may sue for possession after dispossession, but must clearly plead and prove adverse possession, including when the possession became adverse.
material_facts: The plaintiff alternatively relied on the alleged real purchaser’s and then the plaintiff’s long possession as having extinguished the certified purchaser’s title.
The plaint stated that the alleged real purchaser continued in possession but did not allege that the possession became hostile to the certified purchaser or state when it became adverse.
The record contained no evidence of when possession became adverse; references to uninterrupted possession for several years and to acquired title appeared only in the relief clause.
issues.conclusion: Although a person whose possession has matured into title may sue for possession after being dispossessed, the alternative claim failed because adverse possession was not adequately pleaded or proved.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Limitation Act, possession that ripens into title may support a suit for possession after dispossession, independently of the benami transaction. Adverse possession must be adequate in continuity, publicity, and extent, and the pleading must at least identify when possession became adverse so that the start of limitation can be determined. Long possession alone, or a statement in the prayer for relief, is not enough. The Court referred to Sukan v. Krishanand, Sri Bhagwan Singh v. Ram Basi Kuer, and Bishun Dayal v. Kesho Prasad; it noted that Bishun Dayal did not accept an alternative possession-based claim without a proper plea.

rule.if: title_or_possession_suit and adverse_possession_relied_on and hostility_start_not_pleaded and adverse_possession_timing_unproved

predicates.title_or_possession_suit: The plaintiff brings a suit seeking title to property or possession of it.
predicates.adverse_possession_relied_on: The plaintiff relies on possession said to have become adverse to another person’s title.
predicates.hostility_start_not_pleaded: The plaintiff does not clearly plead when possession became hostile to the person whose title is affected.
predicates.adverse_possession_timing_unproved: The evidence does not establish when the possession became adverse.

issues.definition: In a title or possession suit relying on adverse possession, if the plaintiff does not plead when possession became hostile and the evidence does not establish when it became adverse, the alternative adverse-possession claim fails.
